cards.claim: The mass per cent of an element in a compound is the mass of that element in the compound divided by the molar mass of the compound, times 100 (the fraction is split across lines in the PDF text; see equation).
cards.quote: Mass % of an element = mass of that element in the compound 100 molar mass of th × ee compound
cards.equation: ext{Mass \% of an element}= rac{	ext{mass of that element in the compound}}{	ext{molar mass of the compound}}	imes100

cards.claim: An empirical formula gives the simplest whole-number ratio of the atoms in a compound; a molecular formula gives the exact number of each type of atom in a molecule.
cards.quote: An empirical formula represents the simplest whole number ratio of various atoms present in a compound, whereas, the molecular formula shows the exact number of different types of atoms present in a molecule of a compound.

cards.claim: Mass per cent data alone give only the empirical formula; the molecular formula can be obtained only if the molar mass is also known.
cards.quote: If the mass per cent of various elements present in a compound is known, its empirical formula can be determined. Molecular formula can further be obtained if the molar mass is known.

cards.claim: NCERT Problem 1.2: a compound contains 4.07% H, 24.27% C and 71.65% Cl and has molar mass 98.96 g; find its empirical and molecular formulas.
cards.quote: A compound contains 4.07% hydrogen, 24.27% carbon and 71.65% chlorine. Its molar mass is 98.96 g. What are its empirical and molecular formulas?

cards.claim: Result of NCERT Problem 1.2: the empirical formula is CH2Cl, n = 2 (molar mass divided by empirical formula mass), so the molecular formula is C2H4Cl2.
cards.quote: Empirical formula = CH2Cl, n = 2. Hence molecular formula is C2H4Cl2.

cards.claim: When the mole ratios found for an empirical formula are not whole numbers, they are made whole by multiplying all of them by a suitable coefficient.
cards.quote: In case the ratios are not whole numbers, then they may be converted into whole number by multiplying by the suitable coefficient.
